reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4}, so a lone Y (and YYY) fall through to the timezone-offset fallback (zoneStr.replace), producing "+0000"-style output instead of the literal "Y"/"24Y" the test expects.
After the fix, REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone Y stays literal and YYY formats as YY plus a literal Y ("24Y"), matching the expectation.

The PR is a behavior-preserving refactor: the base code already percent-decoded params when "%" was present, and the extracted tryDecodeURIComponent has identical logic, so %20 still decodes to a space.
Same logic as base, just factored into tryDecodeURIComponent; decoding of %20 is unchanged and still works.
At base, reschedule writes to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so reading entry.score/at on the same handle returns the stale pre-reschedule time, not the new time.
The fix adds "@score = at.to_f" after zincrby, so the in-memory handle reflects the new score/time immediately.
The PR only changes Range-header parsing (parseRangesSpecifier); Content-Type charset parsing is untouched, and "text/plain; charset=UTF-8" is standard, working ktor behavior.
Unrelated change to Range parsing; Content-Type charset handling behaves the same as before and correctly reports charset=UTF-8.
The PR only touches ComposerRepository download-error logging, unrelated to zip archiving; Composer archives preserve source mtimes, so extraction should show the release date, not 1980.
Unrelated logging change; repeated archiving yields source-matching timestamps both times.
The PR changes CredentialCache prefix comparison only, unrelated to System.Text.Json; async deserialization of a nullable parent property is standard and works.
Unrelated CredentialCache change; sync and async JSON deserialization of the same payload both succeed and are equivalent.
The PR fixes a cursor FETCH FIRST bug, unrelated to INET; INET <<= ANY containment against a subnet is supported SQL that should parse and return true.
Unrelated cursor fix; INET >>= ANY with an INET[] array is standard containment and should return true.
At base, every NO_PROXY entry is prefixed with a wildcard, turning "::1" into "all://*::1", which later URL parsing cannot interpret and raises, so client construction errors.
The fix recognizes IPv6 and maps "::1" to "all://[::1]", so the client is built without error and bypasses proxying for the loopback.
At base, passing re.DOTALL via flags= (or a compiled pattern) triggers the flag-mismatch ValueError, so the match raises instead of returning [True, False].

The fix restores DOTALL handling; "a.c" with DOTALL matches "a
c" and not "ac" both via flags= and a compiled pattern.
At base, freezing/serializing a chain with a group in the middle leaves stale prev_task/prev_res, so the result tree loses child results for the two parallel groups.
The fix updates prev_task/prev_res after each group, so serialization preserves all four child results across the two groups.

The PR fixes value_terminator specifically when "--" is the FIRST argument; here "--" follows value1/value2, so cmd1 correctly stops at the terminator and cmd2 collects --check, which already worked at base.
The change targets the first-argument case and does not alter the mid-argument "--" scenario, which continues to hand off to the trailing positional.
At base, the late OSC11 response sets background via nvim_set_option_value (autocmd-enabled), so OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands fire as the test expects.
The fix switches to "noautocmd set background=...", which suppresses both OptionSet and ColorScheme, so the test expectation that they fire is no longer met.
The PR only reorders compile-time @derive reading, unrelated to changesets; Ecto validate_required on an omitted field correctly flags the changeset invalid with a "can't be blank" error.
Unrelated derive/Inspect change; required-field validation behavior is unchanged and correctly reports the blank error.
